analysis.title: GS Miller - [GSX] Global Reflections 2 Oct 2026
key_insights: The desk expects the market to favor compounders with durable growth over high-growth cyclicals. Higher rates, oil near $100 and rising energy costs are cited as headwinds to cyclical momentum.
The desk says de-escalation-driven investment narratives are harder to underwrite while the Fed is still tightening, oil is near $100 and 10-year yields are above 5%.
The desk's call on AI over cyclicals (SPXXAI Index) has worked well and it still likes it. It adds that the midterms probably won't be risk positive.
Softer PCE and NFP prints helped the market push out the next Fed hike. The desk sees European exposure as increasingly uncomfortable because fiscal risk is building.

Equity indices keep grinding higher through the rates selloff, held up by AI. Rate-sensitive pockets are under pressure: US Homebuilders basket -17.5% over 3 months, Non-Profitable Tech -11.4% since early July.

Lending Sensitive Equities have underperformed alongside homebuilders and non-profitable tech. Regional Banks have been more resilient than their rates beta implies and could have downside if rates stay elevated.

Lower yields from softer PCE and NFP could drive significant relief in rate-sensitive pockets if sustained. Weak breadth implies scope for a broader beta rally, expressed via the sector/industry-neutral beta basket (GSPUBETA), with the Beta-ex AI pair (GSPUBETX) as a hedge for cautious investors.

Power fundamentals remain intact. GS research sees 108 GW of datacenter power demand by 2030 (23% CAGR off a 2025 base) and a 3.5% CAGR in total US power demand, of which datacenters contribute just over 2.5%.
Equipment demand is described as exceptional. GEV is guiding to 125 GW of backlog plus slot reservation agreements by year end, roughly 6x current capacity.

Power valuations have de-rated: IPPs are down ~30% over 12 months and gas infrastructure names are down ~13% over 3 months. Behind-the-meter supply is expected to reach ~20% of datacenter power demand by 2030 given the 4.5 year interconnection queue and state permitting friction.

Power catalysts the desk is monitoring: FERC ruling on the PJM large-load framework, 3Q earnings, November midterms, and the ERCOT datacenter interconnection audit. It likes owning upside in the theme into year-end.
The desk launched an Asia Battery Backup Units basket (GSXABBUS) covering batteries, modules and energy storage systems. GS research expects the global BBU TAM to expand 23x between 2025 and 2030E.

OAT-Bund spreads are around 150bps with contagion into BTPs this week, which the desk reads as the market pricing broader European sovereign risk. European Banks (SX7E) were hit after an exceptional 18-month rally and significant net length in the trade.

The desk would buy dips in EU Banks if French fiscal risk stays contained, citing a solid structural earnings outlook. It stays cautious on stocks with weak balance sheets and upcoming debt maturities (GSXECLFF).
Investor interest is picking up in equities vulnerable to Euro weakness. The European Domestic vs US exposed pair (GSPEDOAM) has historically been most reactive to EURUSD.

Japan is the standout in Asia, driven by AI leadership, a $140bn AI datacenter push and BoJ normalization gradual enough for equities to absorb. A less hawkish BoJ summary of opinions supported sentiment, and flows favor Japan AI over EM AI beneficiaries.
The desk's favorite Japan AI trade is the Optical Networking basket (GSXAJONE), seen as the key beneficiary of the next leg of AI infrastructure spending.
China Golden Week consumer data is the key watch item when China reopens next week. Another disappointing print would reinforce concerns that stimulus is incremental rather than transformative.

GS economists attribute the widening production-consumption gap in China to a structural pivot to high-tech manufacturing. That supports headline output but is less labor-intensive and negative for employment, household income and consumption.

The desk likes shorts on Asia Consumer Inertia stocks (GSXASWCH). A turnaround in European Luxury (GSXELUXG) needs an inflection in China consumer sentiment, though low valuation and stable EPS momentum have lifted interest ahead of mid-month 3Q updates.

Brazil first-round elections are this weekend. The desk flags Brazil Rate Sensitive (GSBZRATE) as the key equity trade, and a Bolsonaro win would be bullish for equities, particularly rate-sensitive ones.

sector_views.rationale: Demand forecasts keep being revised higher, equipment backlog is strong and valuations have de-rated. The desk likes owning upside into year-end.
Buyers of dips if French fiscal risk stays contained, given a solid structural earnings outlook. Cautious on weak balance sheets and upcoming debt maturities.
Baskets have sold off with rising yields, but sustained lower yields could drive significant relief.
Weak discretionary spend and the risk of AI-enabled switching behavior pressure the group. The desk likes shorts via GSXASWCH.
Japan AI is breaking out from the broader Asia AI datacenter trade, helped by the $140bn datacenter push and gradual BoJ normalization.

earnings_insights: GEV is guiding to 125 GW of backlog plus slot reservation agreements by year end, roughly 6x current capacity. This is company guidance as cited by the desk, not a reported EPS or revenue figure.
3Q earnings are flagged as a catalyst for the power theme. European Luxury names have mid-month 3Q updates ahead, where low valuation and stable EPS momentum have driven a pick-up in interest.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A softer PCE print helped the market push out the next Fed hike and pushed yields lower.
A softer NFP print, together with PCE, helped push out expectations for the next Fed hike and lowered yields.
In a Bolsonaro win scenario, rate-sensitive Brazilian equities could re-rate up to 30% on a 200bp rate cut.

tension_points.bull_case: Softer PCE and NFP are pushing yields lower, which could drive significant relief in homebuilders, non-profitable tech and lending-sensitive equities if sustained. Weak breadth also leaves room for a broader beta rally.
tension_points.bear_case: Regional Banks have been more resilient than their rates beta implies and could have downside if rates remain elevated. Oil near $100 and 10-year yields above 5% keep pressure on the group.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Rates remaining elevated, with 10-year yields staying above 5%.

tension_points.bull_case: The desk would buy dips in EU Banks given a solid structural earnings outlook after the recent selloff.
tension_points.bear_case: OAT-Bund spreads around 150bps and contagion into BTPs show the market pricing broader European sovereign risk, and banks carried significant net length after an exceptional 18-month rally.
tension_points.what_invalidates: French fiscal risk no longer being contained.

tension_points.bull_case: A Bolsonaro win should be bullish for equities, and rate-sensitive equities could re-rate up to 30% in a 200bp rate cut outcome.
tension_points.bear_case: The trade depends on the election result, and the desk does not describe the alternative outcome.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A first-round result other than a Bolsonaro win.
